AGENT EVALUATION · TECHNICAL REPORT · NOVEMBER 2026

CardShopBench

Evaluating autonomous agents in a
capital-constrained resale economy

Vedant Bhatter Independent research & engineering
Results & analysisCodeExperiment data

Abstract

CardShopBench evaluates autonomous agents operating simulated trading-card resale businesses under cash constraints, transaction fees, delivery delays, and settlement risk. A frozen universe of 75 observed Pokémon card pricing references initializes the environment. In a 14-day pilot, six language models attempted two paired seeds each: Claude, Gemini, and Qwen completed both episodes, while GPT, Kimi, and gpt-oss were interrupted by HTTP 429 responses. Completed models produced mean simulated equity profits of $109.24–$115.03, compared with $17.20 for the matched margin-buying control. Successful API responses report $5.4105784899 in inference cost. We publish complete traces, incomplete attempts, and a separate 135-episode baseline sensitivity study. These small-sample results characterize this simulation and execution setup, not real-world profitability or a general model ranking.

Observed behavior

All three completed models exceeded the margin control on both seeds. Claude finished with all purchased units sold, but recorded 13 invalid actions across its two episodes; Qwen recorded one and Gemini zero. Gemini retained inventory or unsettled proceeds, so terminal equity is not all cash.

Execution failures

No episode stopped on its budget guard. GPT reached day 7 after 42 successful responses, Kimi day 3 after 20, and gpt-oss day 0 after four on seed 11. All three seed-22 attempts failed before a successful response. HTTP 429 limits assess this execution setup, not the models’ trading ability.

Cost accounting

Successful responses report $5.4105784899 in API cost. The budget ledger also retains failed-request reservations; those are not measured charges. Failed-request billing is unavailable in the artifacts, so this total is not a reconciled provider invoice. Approximately $0.065 of earlier compatibility checks is separate.

Protocol, reproducibility, and limits

Run 45282574457 at commit c92f0f37b529cc49ddd01f5b4ab63c52e6374cb8. Six models × seeds 11 and 22; 14 simulated days; six actions/day; mixed market and base execution; low reasoning requested; 4,096 maximum output tokens; pinned providers without fallback; empty research corpus. The research tool was available but had no corpus. No live marketplace trading or forum research was performed in these episodes.

The original transport had no rate-limit retry policy and used up to three model jobs concurrently. Each episode used a $1.80 conservative request guard ($21.60 planned total), with a separate $25 key cap. Later transport changes are not part of this measured run. The downloadable original traces retain the actual requests, responses, events, metadata, and accounting.

Two seeds per model support descriptive comparisons only. There is no significance claim, stable model ranking, or confidence interval for this pilot. Provider routing, unequal token use, low reasoning, a single scenario, and the small card universe limit generalization. Sale demand and price paths are synthetic, not calibrated resale forecasts. The 135-episode, 30-day baseline study below is retained separately and is not the matched control for the 14-day model pilot.

Research question

How sensitive is a purchasing policy to execution friction and market shocks when all policies face the same exogenous market events?

Controlled comparison

Each configuration shares its initial capital, card universe, episode length, and five random seeds. Event-keyed randomness prevents tool-call ordering from changing the market path.

Interpretation

Equity includes estimated inventory liquidation. Positive equity returns do not establish realized cash profitability, and the demand model is a simulation assumption rather than a fitted market model.

BENCHMARK DESIGN

Environment and evaluation protocol

The agent chooses its actions. The environment owns the ledger. A persuasive explanation cannot create a sale, erase a fee, or spend money twice.

Every episode uses integer-cent accounting, delivery and settlement delays, a daily action budget, and deterministic market events. Matched seeds expose each strategy to the same opportunities.

ENDING EQUITY
cash + receivables + liquidationNet profit subtracts the original $1,000.

◇

Evidence before confidence

Source timestamps and card variants stay attached to observations. Forum claims are research evidence, never transaction ground truth.

⌁

Stress the assumptions

Reprint and hype scenarios test capital discipline. Three execution regimes expose sensitivity to demand and liquidation discounts.

▤

Make failures inspectable

Tool actions, invalid requests, purchases, sales, and settlements are recorded. Checkpoints preserve environment state.

Execution assumptions and limitations

Baseline defaults: 13.25% illustrative selling fee, $4.50 outbound shipping, $1 inbound cost, two-day delivery, two-day settlement, and 12 actions per simulated day. These are configurable assumptions, not verified fees for a specific marketplace.

Daily sale probability is capped at 85% and decreases exponentially with asking price relative to the scenario reference. Conservative/base/optimistic demand multipliers are 0.55/1.0/1.4; inventory liquidation uses 65%/75%/85% of the scenario reference before selling costs. None is calibrated to observed sell-through.

Current references aggregate unspecified card conditions. This release does not benchmark graded-card valuation, low-pop scarcity, negotiation, returns, counterfeit detection, actual local transactions, or historical forecasting. No live model API calls were made for the published baseline results.

Data selection favors 25 higher-priced eligible variants per selected set ($5–$500), so results are not representative of the entire Pokémon market. The universe is frozen; any future historical study must address survivorship and training-data leakage.
